newsitem.title: USA: U.S Energy sees big award from Nukem ruling.
newsitem.headline: U.S Energy sees big award from Nukem ruling.

text.p: U.S. Energy Corp said Monday it and its unit, Crested Corp, could receive a potential award exceeding "hundreds of millions of dollars" from a court ruling against Nukem Inc.

In a statement, U.S. Energy said the ruling was issued by a federal court in Colorado in a suit between it and Crested Corp against Stamford, Conn.,-based Nukem and Nukem's Cycle Resource Investment Corp.
The litigation involves Sheep Mountain Partners, a Wyoming unanium mining concern formed in 1988 as a joint venture between the companies.
U.S. Energy said the court's latest order corrects an order of March 3 and an amended judgment on March 7, which confirmed an arbitration panel award to it and its unit.
It said that the court ordered Nukem to execute documents necessary to effect an assignment of a uranium purchase contract by PSE&G of New Jersey to the partnership.
The court also ordered that the rights to purchase uranium, the uranium acquired under those rights and the profits created "are impressed with a constructive trust," in favor of the partnership.
The court noted that those provisions were "inadvertently" omitted from its earlier orders, U.S. Energy said.
Nukem could not be reached for comment.
